### Observed differences

- Three activities that were essentially absent earlier appear in the later window: A19 occurred in 0 of 200 traces before and in about 38 in 100 later; A20 rose from about 0.5 in 100 to about 30 in 100; A25 from 0 to about 35 in 100. Each typically occurs once, around a third of the way into the trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- The direct link from A41 to A26 largely disappeared: earlier, about 82 in 100 observed A41→A26 pairs were one step apart (about 18 in 100 two steps); in the later window only about 1 in 100 is directly adjacent, while about 83 in 100 are two steps and about 14 in 100 three steps apart. [LAG001]
- A41's outgoing transitions were redirected accordingly: earlier about 82 in 100 went to A26; in the later window about 33 go to A19, about 30 to A25 and about 24 to A20, with only about 2 in 100 still going directly to A26. [DIR004]
- When present, A19 and A25 lead almost exclusively to A26 (about 95 and about 90 in 100 of their observed outgoing transitions, respectively). [DIR002, DIR003]
- Ordering relations changed consistently: earlier, A26 always appeared without A19, A20 or A25; in the later window A41 precedes the respective activity and that activity precedes A26 in roughly 28–38 in 100 traces for each of the three. [REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- The three new activities are near-exclusive alternatives: any pair of them co-occurs in only about 1–2 in 100 later traces, and about 99 in 100 later traces contain exactly one of them. [REL001, REL002, REL005]
- A26 still occurs in every trace in both windows, at a slightly later relative position (median about 0.36 vs about 0.39 of trace length). [POS004]
- A02 no longer routes to A26: about 26 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A26 earlier, none do in the later window; this rests on few observations (about 35 vs 44 outgoing transitions). [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The screening produced 21 qualifying items against about 0.52 expected without change in the control-flow family — roughly forty times the chance expectation — so the set of differences cannot be explained by random sampling alone. The evidence supports the hypothesis that a new intermediate step was inserted between A41 and A26: in the later window, most cases run A41 → one of A19, A20 or A25 → A26, where the three activities act as near-exclusive per-case alternatives, whereas earlier A41 led directly to A26 and the three activities were not observed. The supporting signs are direct and mutually consistent: the appearance of the three activities, the redirection of A41's outgoing transitions away from A26 towards them, their outgoing transitions leading back to A26, the before/after ordering relations, and the A41→A26 distance shifting from one to two steps. Because the occurrence, direction, relation and lag items largely describe the same underlying trace behaviour, they converge on one change rather than independently confirming it. Limitations: no outgoing profile was measured for A20, so its link to A26 rests on ordering evidence only; positions are event positions rather than clock times; and about 14 in 100 later cases show a three-step gap (with about 18 in 100 earlier cases already at two steps), so additional unobserved intermediates or entry routes into the new step cannot be ruled out.

Other differences: A02's routing to A26 disappeared, though on weak support; A26's position shifted slightly later, consistent with the insertion. [DIR001, POS004]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- Two windows, 200 traces each.
- Screening: 104 units tested, 21 items qualified, 0.52 expected by chance. That's about 40 times the chance expectation — far more than an unchanged process would produce. So we're beyond "insufficient evidence" at the screening level. All items are control-flow family; 21 items vs 0.52 expected in that family.

Now let me understand the behavioural story.

Key activities: A19, A20, A25 (new/rare before, common after), A26, A41 (common before, still common after but relationship changed), A02.

OCC001: A19 — before: 0 participation (0 traces), after: 38% participation (76/200 traces). Increased.
OCC002: A20 — before: 0.5% (1 trace), after: 29.5% (59 traces). Increased.
OCC003: A25 — before: 0, after: 34.5% (69 traces). Increased.

DIR002: A19's outgoing transitions — before: empty (A19 never observed), after: 94.7% of A19's outgoing transitions go to A26 (support after = 76 traces containing A19). So A19 → A26 is the dominant edge.
DIR003: A25's outgoing — before empty, after: 90% to A26 (support 70).
DIR004: A41's outgoing — before: 81.7% to A26 (support 202 outgoing transitions across traces containing A41); after: only 1.5% to A26, redistributed to A19 (33%), A25 (30%), A20 (23.6%). So A41 now leads to A19/A25/A20 instead of A26.
DIR001: A02's outgoing — before: 25.7% to A26; after: A26 component 0 (dropped), redistributed across many activities including A16 (18%), A45 (16%), A15 (11%), A47 (9%), A19 (4.5%), A25 (2.3%), A20 (2.3%). Support before 35, after 44 outgoing transitions — small support, so weak-ish but the drop of A26 from ~26% to 0 is notable.

POS001: A19 position — before absent, after appears around 35-37% of trace length (median 0.346).
POS002: A20 — before 1 trace at position 0.333; after median 0.367. Slight shift.
POS003: A25 — before absent, after median 0.357.
POS004: A26 — present in all traces both windows; position shifted slightly later (median 0.36 → 0.387). Small change.

REL items:
REL003 (A19, A26): before — A26 always present, A19 never: B_only = 100%. After — cooccurrence 38%, B_only 62%, and when together, A19 before A26 in 37.5% of traces. So A19 now precedes A26 in ~38 in 100 traces.
REL004 (A19, A41): before — B_only (A41 only) 100%. After — cooccurrence 38%, B_only 62%, B_before_A 37.5%: A41 before A19.
REL006 (A20, A26): before B_only 99.5%; after cooccurrence 29.5%, A20 before A26 28.5%.
REL007 (A20, A41): before B_only 99.5%; after cooccurrence 29.5%, B_before_A 28%: A41 before A20.
REL008 (A25, A26): before B_only 100%; after cooccurrence 34.5%, A25 before A26 32.5%.
REL009 (A25, A41): before B_only 100%; after cooccurrence 34.5%, B_before_A 33%: A41 before A25.
REL001 (A19, A20): before neither 99.5%; after neither 33.5%, A_only 37%, B_only 28.5%, cooccurrence 1% — A19 and A20 rarely occur together; they're mostly alternatives (each appears without the other).
REL002 (A19, A25): before neither 100%; after neither 29%, A_only 36.5%, B_only 33%, cooccurrence 1.5% — again mostly alternatives.
REL005 (A20, A25): before neither 99.5%; after neither 36.5%, A_only 29%, B_only 34% — alternatives.

LAG001 (A41 → A26 lag): before — gap of 1 step in 82.5% of cases, gap 2 in 17.5%. After — gap 1 in only 1.2%, gap 2 in 83.4%, gap 3 in 14.1%. So the direct A41 → A26 adjacency mostly disappeared; when both occur, they're now further apart.

So the story: In the before window, A41 was followed directly by A26 (82.5% within one step). A19, A20, A25 were essentially absent. In the after window, A19, A20, A25 appear in roughly 30-38% of traces, positioned around a third into the trace, each leading predominantly to A26 (A19→A26 ~95% of its outgoing, A25→A26 ~90%), and A41 now leads to A19/A25/A20 (together ~87% of its outgoing) instead of directly to A26. A19, A20, A25 are largely mutually exclusive (alternatives) — each trace tends to include one of them, not several. A26 still occurs in all traces, slightly later in position.

So the hypothesis: a new intermediate stage was inserted between A41 and A26 — one of A19, A20, or A25 (chosen per case, as alternatives) now sits between them. Before: A41 → A26 directly. After: A41 → (A19 | A20 | A25) → A26.

Check consistency: A41's outgoing after: A19 33%, A25 30%, A20 23.6% — sums to ~87%. A19's outgoing: A26 94.7%. A25's outgoing: A26 90%. A20's outgoing isn't in DIR evidence... Actually DIR items are A02, A19, A25, A41. A20's outgoing not shown. But REL006 shows A20 before A26 in 28.5% of traces, consistent with A20 → A26.

Participation: A19 38%, A20 29.5%, A25 34.5% — sums to ~102%, and cooccurrence among them is ~1-1.5%, so they're nearly disjoint alternatives covering essentially all traces? Wait: A_only + B_only + neither for REL001 (A19,A20): 37 + 28.5 + 33.5 = 99. So in ~66% of traces at least one of A19/A20 appears. Hmm, but A41's outgoing to these three sums to 87% of its outgoing transitions. A41 occurs in all traces presumably (support 202/200 — outgoing transitions counted, 202 in before, 203 after; traces containing A41 ~ all).

Actually wait — does A41 always lead to one of A19/A20/A25? 33+30+23.6 = 86.6%. Plus small others. Before, A41 → A26 was 81.7%.

Hmm, but A26 still occurs in 100% of traces after. And A26's position shifted slightly later (median 0.36 → 0.387), consistent with an inserted activity before it.

LAG001: A41→A26 within 5 steps: before gap 1 (82.5%), after gap 2 (83.4%) — consistent with one activity inserted between them.

So the hypothesis is well supported: an optional intermediate step (one of A19/A20/A25, mutually exclusive alternatives) was inserted between A41 and A26 in roughly 87% of traces (or appears in ~30-38% of traces each). Actually, since the three are nearly disjoint and each occurs in ~30-38% of traces, together they cover ~102% minus overlaps ~ nearly all traces? Let's compute: A19 38%, A20 29.5%, A25 34.5%. Pairwise cooccurrence ~1-1.5% each. Union ≈ 38+29.5+34.5 − 3×~1 ≈ 99%. So essentially every trace in the after window contains exactly one of A19/A20/A25. And A41 precedes it, which precedes A26.

Wait, but before, A41→A26 gap 1 in 82.5% and gap 2 in 17.5%. After, gap 2 in 83.4%, gap 3 in 14%. So in the after window, A41 and A26 are separated by exactly one activity in ~83% of cases — the inserted A19/A20/A25. In ~14% gap 3. Hmm, and in before, 17.5% had gap 2 — maybe something else between.

But wait — is the inserted activity always between A41 and A26? REL003: A19 before A26 in 37.5% of traces (cooccurrence 38%). REL004: A41 before A19 in 37.5%. So A41 → A19 → A26 in ~37.5% of traces. Similarly A41 → A25 → A26 in ~33%, A41 → A20 → A26 in ~28%. Total ~98-99%. Yes! That's a consistent chain.

So the main hypothesis: a new step, one of A19, A20, A25 (selected per case as near-exclusive alternatives), was inserted between A41 and A26, so A41 now reaches A26 through this intermediate step instead of directly. This is a structural change: activities added (A19, A20, A25 became active), and the direct A41→A26 edge was replaced by A41→intermediate→A26.

This is NOT a "change in how often existing paths are taken" — it's insertion of new activities (they were absent before). The condition for path-frequency shift doesn't apply; this is addition of activities / a bypass in reverse (a group inserted). The hypothesis type: activities added / new intermediate step inserted.

Support level: The screening comparison: 21 items vs 0.52 expected — many times larger, so chance can't explain the whole set. Directness: OCC shows A19/A20/A25 absent→present; DIR shows A41's outgoing shifted from A26 to these three, and these three's outgoing goes to A26; REL shows ordering A41 before intermediate before A26; LAG shows the A41→A26 gap shifted from 1 to 2 steps. This is direct, consistent relational evidence. So "Supported hypothesis".

Competing explanations: Could it be that A19/A20/A25 are executed somewhere else entirely and the A41→A26 link just weakened for another reason? The REL and LAG evidence ties them into the A41→A26 span directly. One limitation: we don't have DIR for A20, so A20→A26 is inferred from REL006 ordering (A20 before A26 in 28.5% of traces) rather than a direct edge. Also, position evidence is relative (event positions), not clock time. Also, in ~14% of after-window cases the gap is 3 steps, and before ~17.5% had gap 2, so there may be other unobserved intermediates. Also the small residual A41→A26 direct share (1.5% after) — nearly gone.

Also DIR001 (A02): A02's outgoing to A26 dropped from ~26% to 0, redistributed widely. Support is small (35 and 44 outgoing transitions), so this is weaker. Report under other differences.

POS004: A26 slightly later position — consistent with insertion, minor.
